annotator.notes: The student incorrectly counts the 'X' marks as the people attending rather than those absent. The tutor corrects this misconception through questioning.

task_context.problem_statement:
Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: On each day but Wednesday, only one person can attend a meeting. On Wednesday, two people can. Thus, the day on which the most people can attend a meeting is $\boxed{\text{Wednesday}}.$

messages.content:
Hi, I'm stuck on this problem. Can you just tell me the answer? Here it is:

Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}

I can't give you the answer directly, but I'd be happy to help you figure it out! Let's start by looking closely at what the 'X' marks in the table actually represent. According to the problem, what does an 'X' mean for a specific person on a specific day?

It means they are available to attend the meeting on that day. So, if I look at the table, Friday has the most X's with two of them (Bill and Carl), so Friday must be the day the most people can attend.

I see how you arrived at that, but let's re-read the first sentence of the problem very carefully. It says: 'Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would NOT be able to attend.' 

Based on that, does an 'X' mean they are available or unavailable?
Oh, I totally misread it. The 'X' means they can't make it. My bad. So I need to look for the day with the fewest X's instead?

That's exactly right. Since the 'X' represents an absence, the day with the fewest 'X' marks will be the day when the maximum number of people are actually available. Why don't you try counting the marks for each day again?

Okay, let me check. 
Mon: 2 X's
Tues: 2 X's
Wed: 1 X
Thurs: 2 X's
Fri: 2 X's

Since Wednesday only has one X, that means only one person is missing, so more people can attend then than on any other day. Is that the right way to solve it?

Your logic is spot on. You correctly identified that fewer absences lead to higher attendance. Since you've analyzed the counts for every day and compared them, you have all the information needed to name the final day.
